content.user_title: Plan Agile Sprints With Clear Capacity
content.value_statement: Sprint planning can fail when backlog scope, team capacity, and goals are unclear. This skill guides structured planning, prioritization, and review workflows.
actual_capabilities: Guides sprint planning sessions with backlog review, scope selection, and sprint goal definition.
Explains RICE, MoSCoW, WSJF, and value-versus-effort prioritization methods.
Provides a sprint plan template for goals, capacity, backlog items, risks, and approvals.
Suggests capacity and velocity calculations using recent sprint history and team availability.
Offers examples for planning, backlog prioritization, mid-sprint checks, and sprint close activities.
Recommends delegation points for GitHub issue work, research, and plan validation.
limitations: Referenced helper scripts and reference files are not included in the scanned package.
GitHub issue and project actions require available GitHub CLI access and user approval.
Velocity and capacity advice depends on accurate sprint history and team availability data.
The skill provides planning guidance, not a complete project management system.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Sprint Plan
use_cases.description: Create a sprint goal, capacity estimate, backlog scope, risks, and approval checklist before planning starts.

use_cases.title: Prioritize Product Backlogs
use_cases.description: Apply RICE, MoSCoW, WSJF, or value-versus-effort scoring to compare candidate work items.

use_cases.title: Review Sprint Health
use_cases.description: Assess progress, blockers, burndown signals, and scope decisions during an active sprint.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Basic Sprint
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan our next sprint. Ask for team size, sprint length, backlog items, capacity limits, and the main product goal.

prompt_templates.title: Prioritize a Backlog
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these backlog items and rank them with RICE and MoSCoW. Explain the scoring assumptions and sprint fit.

prompt_templates.title: Check Sprint Progress
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this sprint status. Identify blockers, scope risk, burndown concerns, and recommended adjustments for the team.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Full Sprint Operating Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a complete sprint plan with goals, capacity, prioritized scope, dependencies, metrics, ceremonies, risks, and retrospective follow-up actions.

output_examples.input: Plan Sprint 6 for a four-person team with ten work days and thirty-five target points.
output_examples.output: A sprint plan with a primary goal, capacity estimate, prioritized backlog, risks, ceremonies, and approval checklist.

output_examples.input: Prioritize our backlog before planning starts.
output_examples.output: A ranked backlog grouped by priority, scoring rationale, sprint candidates, and items to defer.

output_examples.input: How is the current sprint tracking after day seven?
output_examples.output: A progress assessment with completed points, remaining work, blockers, burndown risk, and scope recommendations.

best_practices: Use recent sprint history and known availability before setting a commitment target.
Keep one clear sprint goal and choose backlog items that support it.
Reserve capacity for unknowns, urgent defects, reviews, and coordination work.
anti_patterns: Do not fill a sprint to full theoretical capacity without a buffer.
Do not add mid-sprint work unless equivalent scope is removed or explicitly approved.
Do not treat velocity as a cross-team performance comparison.

faq.question: Does this skill create sprint boards automatically?
faq.answer: It can suggest GitHub workflow steps, but board changes require available tools, permissions, and user approval.

faq.question: Can it calculate team capacity?
faq.answer: Yes. It guides capacity estimates using team size, sprint length, availability, holidays, and recent velocity.

faq.question: Which prioritization methods are included?
faq.answer: It describes RICE, MoSCoW, WSJF, and value-versus-effort methods for backlog planning.

faq.question: Does the package include working Python scripts?
faq.answer: No evidence found in the scanned files. The skill references scripts, but they are not included in this package.

faq.question: Can it support mid-sprint decisions?
faq.answer: Yes. It helps review progress, blockers, scope changes, and possible adjustments during a sprint.

faq.question: Is it only for Scrum teams?
faq.answer: No. The guidance fits Scrum-style sprints and can also support other iterative planning processes.
